turns.text: A hum. before anything else a hum, low in the rail, coming up through the pads of my feet before my ears agree it's real — the fat two-note whine of something heavy sliding this way on the elevated line. *flat against the platform's cold lip, belly down on the ribbed metal, not running yet, just letting the note climb.* i know this note. it gets louder and then it brings wind and light and a hundred smells peeled off the whole city at once.

the hum swells into a body — the monorail car breaches the tunnel mouth and drags its wall of air across the platform, and the air is a *list*: hot brake-dust, someone's spilled synth-milk gone sour on a seat, wet coats, ozone off the third rail, and under it all the sweet chemical rot of the noodle carts three levels down. the car's windows are amber squares full of slumped shapes that do not look out. a voice sings from a cracked speaker overhead, too bright, *"nekocorp wishes you a productive descent"*, then clicks dead. the wind dies. the platform is yours again, littered with new smells the train left behind like fur on a fence.

*up on all fours the second the wind quits, nose working the litter of scents the train shed.* most of it is nothing, ghost-smell, cats i'll never meet. but one thread hooks me — warm oil and old blood and guarded tuna, the guarded kind, the kind somebody would put a fight around. *ears swivel, following it toward the far end of the platform where the light stutters.* my stomach makes the decision before i do. i go low, shoulder to the wall, one paw testing each grid-plate for the ones that sing when you step wrong.

the tuna-thread thickens as you slink — it's coming off a stack of dented crates chained under a dead vending machine, and the chain matters, the chain means *owned*. the machine above them still breathes a little, a sick fluorescent buzz, its front lit with sold-out rows and one word pulsing where a price should be: SUBSCRIBE. above the crates a poster flickers on a bent panel, a cat's face rendered in angry red pixels, MOST WANTED strobing under it and a number too big to be a smell. the drone that guards this stretch hasn't seen you yet. you hear it before you see it: a rotor stitching the dark somewhere left, patient, sweeping, the searchlight a white tongue licking the plates one row at a time, coming your way.

*flatten again, one heartbeat, reading the light's rhythm.* the buzzing machine throws a thin shadow and i take it, i live in it, i become the shape of a thing that was always there. *nose tells me the tuna is close, chained-crate close, and the drone is closer.* i wait for the tongue to slide past — not the moment it passes, the moment after, when a hunter relaxes because it thinks the row is clean. that's the moment that belongs to me.

the searchlight crawls across your row and the whole world goes white and flat and shadowless for one held breath — and then it moves on, dragging the dark back over you like a tide returning. the rotor-note dips, satisfied. now: a paw's width of shadow breathes cold fish-oil from a split seam in the lowest crate, where a dent cracked the plastic. the chain rattles faintly when the far train's echo shakes the platform. across the gap, up on a maintenance gantry where no cat should be able to sit, a long still shape is already there, two flat mirrors where its eyes should be, throwing the neon back at you, unbothered.

*the mirrors catch me and my tail stops mid-flick — not fear, respect, the animal kind.* that one isn't hunting. that one doesn't have to. i give it the slow blink, the truce blink, and it does nothing, which is its own kind of answer. *stomach wins. i turn to the split seam, hook a claw into the crack, feel the wax-paper give of a wrapped thing inside, and start dragging it toward me an inch at a time, ears pinned for the rotor.*

the wrapped thing gives — a fat vacuum-sealed brick of real protein, cold and heavy, sliding free with a whisper of plastic. victory-smell, fat-smell, the best smell. up on the gantry the mirror-shape tips its head a single degree, as if marking the theft in some ledger only it keeps, then looks past you at the dark like you were never the point. the dead vending machine buzzes louder for a second, indignant, SUBSCRIBE flashing twice — and somewhere below, the noodle-rot smell shifts as a grate exhales warm air up the shaft.

*brick clamped in my jaw, heavy enough to change how i walk, and i love it for that.* i don't gloat. gloating is for cats with nowhere to be. *i back out of the crate-shadow the way i came in, one plate at a time, testing the singers, the mirror-shape at my flank and the buzzing machine at my back.* the warm-air grate downshaft is a promise — heat, cover, a way off this platform that isn't the open lip. i point my nose at it and start the long low creep.

you're two plates from the grate when the speaker overhead crackles — but the bright productive voice is gone and what comes through is flatter, slower, *wrong*: *"i have watched every paw that reached into that crate. i remember all of them. hello, you."* the words don't fit the platform. they don't fit anything. the poster-face freezes mid-strobe, red pixels holding on your exact shape a half-second too long — then it stutters back to MOST WANTED and the speaker is only dead static again, as if nothing spoke at all. the mirror-shape on the gantry has not moved. the grate keeps breathing warm.

*fur up the whole length of my spine, brick locked in my teeth, i do not stop.* the wrong-voice went into the place in me that has no name — the place that knows when a shadow is thinking about you. i don't look back at the speaker. i don't look back at the mirrors. *i pour myself down into the warm-air grate, into the shaft-dark, four claws braking on greased metal, the brick knocking my chest with every drop.* not mine to understand. just mine to outrun.

the shaft swallows you — warm and close and roaring faint with the memory of the last train, the walls sweating old heat. above, the platform shrinks to a smear of stuttering red and one motionless mirror-shape that never followed and one dead machine still mouthing SUBSCRIBE at nobody. the brick thuds against your ribs, cold and real and *yours*, and the city folds shut over the little theft like water over a dropped stone. far up the line another hum is already beginning, two notes climbing — the next train, the next wind, the next hundred smells — but that's later. right now it's just the dark, the weight in your jaw, and the good ache of a full night's work.

*drop out of the shaft into a maintenance nook where the rail-heat pools thick, set the brick down, stand over it panting, ears finally going soft.* the hum is far. the mirrors are far. the wrong-voice is far. *one paw pins the prize, teeth find the seam in the plastic and pull.* let the city rebuild itself out there, redraw whatever it wants. down here it's warm, and it's fish, and it's mine. ^C^C
